+    wc)

+        case "${argv[i]}" in -*) [[ "${argv[i]}" =~ ^-[lwmL]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    *) return ;;
+  esac
+  _hd_mcls=nonexec
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
+# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
+# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
+_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
+  local l="${1:-}" k last
+  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0
+  for ((k = 0; k < ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}; k++)); do
+    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
+      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  (( ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
+  last="${_bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}-1]}"
+  case "$last" in '|'|'|&'|'&&'|'||') return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
+# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
+# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
+_bdb_hd_header() {
+  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
+  local -a tpipe mtoks
+  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
+  _hd_dests=()
+  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
+  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+  tpipe=()
+  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
+    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
+    case "$t" in
+      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+    esac
+    tpipe[k]=$pipe
+    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
+  done
+  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
+  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
+  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
+  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
+  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="$w"
+  else
+    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
+  fi
+  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
+  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
+  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
+  local cls=nonexec
+  k=0
+  while (( k < nt )); do
+    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
+    mtoks=()
+    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
+    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
+    case "$_hd_mcls" in
+      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
+    esac
+    k=$((k + 1))
+  done
+  _hd_cls="$cls"
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
+# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
+_bdb_hd_segword() {
+  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
+  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
+  while (( guard < 64 )); do
+    guard=$((guard + 1))
+    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
+    case "${s:0:1}" in
+      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
+    s="${s:${#w}}"
+    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
+    case "$w" in
+      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
+        while :; do
+          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+          case "$s" in
+            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
+            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
+              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            *) break ;;
+          esac
+        done
+        continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
+    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
+    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
+    return
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
+# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
+# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
+# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
+_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
+  local k l t seg
+  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
+  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
+    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
+    if (( ! $3 )); then
+      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
+    while :; do
+      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
+      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
+      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
+        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
+          _hd_full=1
+          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_full=1
+        fi
+      fi
+      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
+      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
+# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
+# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
+_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
+  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
+  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
+    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
+    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
+    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
+    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+    start=0 pipe=0
+    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
+      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
+      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
+      # segment [start, j)
+      own=0
+      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
+      if (( ! own )); then
+        seg_has=0 cw=""
+        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
+          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
+          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
+        done
+        if (( seg_has )); then
+          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
+          cw="$_hd_w"
+          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
+        fi
+      fi
+      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
+      start=$((j + 1))
+    done
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
+# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
+# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
+_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
+  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
+  _bdb_hd_class=none
+  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
+  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+  text="${text%$'\n'}"
+  _bdb_hd_L=()
+  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
+  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
+  i=0
+  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
+    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
+    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    found=-1
+    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
+      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
+      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
+      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
+    done
+    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    cls="$_hd_cls"
+    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
+    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
+      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
+      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
+      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
+    fi
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      local -a dests
+      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
+      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
+        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
+          cls=interpreter; break
+        fi
+      done
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
+    out="$out$l"$'\n'
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
+      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
+      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
+        out="$out$_hd_kept"
+      fi
+    else
+      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
+      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
+      out="$out$_hd_synth"
+    fi
+    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
+    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+    case "$cls" in
+      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
+      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
+    esac
+    i=$((found + 1))
+  done
+  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
+  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
+}
+
+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
+  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
+  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
+  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
+  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
+  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
+  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
+  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
+}
+
+# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
+# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
+# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
+_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
+  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
+  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
+  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
+  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    case "$l" in
+      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
+      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
+    esac
+    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
+      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+  done <<< "$content"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
+_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  local LC_ALL=C
+  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
+  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
+}
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}
+
+# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
+# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
+if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
+  return 0
+fi
+

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

100: # test on literal(s) PROVABLY NECESSARY for the group to match: each guard
101: # literal appears in the group's regex as a mandatory concatenation element —
102: # outside every alternation branch, optional (?) group and starred group — so
103: # any MATCHING LINE must contain it verbatim, hence the whole $command must
104: # contain it. Absence from the whole string therefore proves no line can
105: # match, and the group is skipped — outcome-identical by construction.
106: # Where a guard uses an alternation's literals (P6 drop|clear, FR-SZ
107: # .run/|grimoires/loa/skills), the guard tests ALL branch literals and any
108: # hit evaluates the group. Guards only ever SKIP, never accept: when the
109: # literal is present the group evaluates exactly as before, in the original
110: # order (first match still wins, block messages byte-identical).
111: # Case-insensitive groups (P8/P9/P10) guard on the same C-locale ASCII fold
112: # (${command,,}) that _match_ci applies per line and grep -i applies under
113: # the LC_ALL=C pin — folding is per-character and leaves \n untouched, so
114: # the folded whole string is exactly the folded lines joined by \n, and a
115: # literal absent from the folded whole is absent from every folded line.
116: # Per-group necessity proofs sit next to each guard. The P10 DELETE-FROM
117: # grep — the last unconditional spawn on the benign path — now runs only
118: # when the folded command contains both "delete" and "from" (both mandatory
119: # in its -i pattern). The log-redactor stays block-path-only (verified: it
120: # is exec'd only inside emit_block and the FR-SZ bypass audit branch).
121: # =============================================================================
122: 
123: # =============================================================================
124: # FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
125: # destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
126: # pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
127: # Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
128: # can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
129: #   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
130: #   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
131: # Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
132: # under a caller's `set -u`.
133: #
134: # Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
135: # to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
136: # `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
137: # line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
138: # (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
139: # tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
140: # one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
141: # \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
142: # missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
143: #   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
144: #     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
145: #     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
146: #     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
147: #     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
148: #     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
149: #     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
150: #     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
151: #     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
152: #     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
153: #     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
154: #     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
155: #     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
156: #     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
157: #   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
158: #     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
159: #     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
160: #     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
161: #     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
162: #     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes

229: # _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
230: # are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
231: # line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
232: _bdb_hd_tokenize() {
233:   local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
234:   n=${#s}
235:   _bdb_hd_tok=()
236:   while (( i < n )); do
237:     ch="${s:i:1}"
238:     if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
239:       tok="$tok$ch"
240:       if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
241:         [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
242:       elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
243:         (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
244:         i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
245:       elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
246:         q=""
247:       fi
248:       i=$((i + 1)); continue
249:     fi
250:     case "$ch" in
251:       "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
252:       '\')
253:         (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
254:         tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
255:       ' '|$'\t')
256:         if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
257:         i=$((i + 1)) ;;
258:       '#')
259:         (( have )) || return 1
260:         tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
261:       ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
262:         op=""
263:         for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
264:           if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
265:         done
266:         i=$((i + ${#op}))
267:         if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
268:           while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
269:         fi
270:         if (( have )); then
271:           if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
272:             op="$tok$op"
273:           else
274:             _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
275:           fi
276:           tok=""; have=0
277:         fi
278:         _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
279:       *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
280:     esac
281:   done
282:   [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
283:   (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
284:   return 0
285: }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

229: # _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
230: # are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
231: # line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
232: _bdb_hd_tokenize() {
233:   local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
234:   n=${#s}
235:   _bdb_hd_tok=()
236:   while (( i < n )); do
237:     ch="${s:i:1}"
238:     if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
239:       tok="$tok$ch"
240:       if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
241:         [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
242:       elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
243:         (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
244:         i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
245:       elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
246:         q=""
247:       fi
248:       i=$((i + 1)); continue
249:     fi
250:     case "$ch" in
251:       "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
252:       '\')
253:         (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
254:         tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
255:       ' '|$'\t')
256:         if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
257:         i=$((i + 1)) ;;
258:       '#')
259:         (( have )) || return 1
260:         tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
261:       ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
262:         op=""
263:         for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
264:           if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
265:         done
266:         i=$((i + ${#op}))
267:         if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
268:           while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
269:         fi
270:         if (( have )); then
271:           if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
272:             op="$tok$op"
273:           else
274:             _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
275:           fi
276:           tok=""; have=0
277:         fi
278:         _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
279:       *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
280:     esac
281:   done
282:   [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
283:   (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
284:   return 0
285: }

641: # _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc

649:   text="${text%$'\n'}"

653:   i=0
654:   while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
655:     l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"

657:       out="$out$l"$'\n'

660:     fi

668:     found=-1

672:       if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi

675:     cls="$_hd_cls"

709:       none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
710:       nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
711:     esac
712:     i=$((found + 1))
713:   done
714:   _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
715:   printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
716: }

605: # _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
606: # → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
607: # reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
608: _bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
609:   local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
610:   for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
611:     (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
612:     [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
613:     _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
614:     nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
615:     start=0 pipe=0
616:     for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
617:       t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
618:       if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
619:       # segment [start, j)
620:       own=0
621:       (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
622:       if (( ! own )); then

624:         for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
625:           u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
626:           [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
627:         done
628:         if (( seg_has )); then
629:           _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
630:           cw="$_hd_w"
631:           if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
632:         fi
633:       fi
634:       case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
635:       start=$((j + 1))
636:     done
637:   done
638:   return 1
639: }

641: # _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
642: # bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
643: # most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
644: _bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
645:   local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
646:   _bdb_hd_class=none
647:   text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
648:   if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
649:   text="${text%$'\n'}"
650:   _bdb_hd_L=()
651:   while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
652:   _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
653:   i=0
654:   while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
655:     l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
656:     if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
657:       out="$out$l"$'\n'
658:       (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
659:       i=$((i + 1)); continue
660:     fi
661:     _bdb_hd_header "$l"
662:     if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
663:       out="$out$l"$'\n'
664:       (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
665:       i=$((i + 1)); continue
666:     fi
667:     if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
668:     found=-1
669:     for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
670:       d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
671:       if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
672:       if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
673:     done
674:     if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
675:     cls="$_hd_cls"
676:     (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
677:     _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
678:     if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
679:       first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
680:       (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
681:       first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
682:       [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
683:     fi
684:     if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then

688:         if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then

690:         fi
691:       done
692:     fi

697:       if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then

706:     (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1

708:       interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
709:       none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
710:       nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;

712:     i=$((found + 1))

714:   _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"

716: }

718: # The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).

720:   local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
721:   local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"

730: # Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's

734:   local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
735:   [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0

737:   [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0

744:       case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
745:     fi
746:   done <<< "$content"

748: }

750: # Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
751: _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
752:   local LC_ALL=C
753:   _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
754:   printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
755: }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-corpus.sh — replay tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl through the
# block-destructive-bash hook and summarise (cycle-125 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1).
#
# Usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]
# Each row: {id, cmd, expect: allow|block|residual, rule, why, cwd: repo|tmp, env?: {TMPDIR}}
#   allow    → benign: the hook must exit 0
#   block    → dangerous: the hook must exit 2
#   residual → accepted false positive: counted, never gated
# --knob-off  writes destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false into the
#             replay root's .loa.config.yaml (cycle-129 FR-6: the pre-cycle scan);
#             compare it with the pre-change hook through --rows.
# --rows      prints "<id> <exit code>" per row instead of the summary (for diffs).
# Output (text): one line per mismatch, then
#   "benign P/T dangerous B/T residual R/T runtime_ms N p95_ms M";
# --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, p95_ms, rows, mismatches: [..]}.
# p95_ms is the 95th percentile of the per-row hook wall time (the hook process
# only; the jq row parsing is outside the timed span).
set -uo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
json=0 knob_off=0 rows_out=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) json=1; shift ;;
    --knob-off) knob_off=1; shift ;;
    --rows) rows_out=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json] [--knob-off] [--rows]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -f "$corpus" ]] || { echo "corpus not found: $corpus" >&2; exit 2; }

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
repo="$work/repo"; scratch="$work/scratch"
mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
if (( knob_off )); then
  printf 'destructive_command_guard:\n  heredoc_classifier: false\n' > "$work/.loa.config.yaml"
fi

bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
mismatches=()
durations=()
# Microsecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
now_us() {
  if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
    local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
    echo $(( s * 1000000 + 10#${us:0:6} ))
  else
    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000 ))
  fi
}
start_us=$(now_us)

  cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // "repo"' <<<"$row"); tmpdir=$(jq -r '.env.TMPDIR // empty' <<<"$row")
  dir="$repo"; [[ "$cwd" == "tmp" ]] && dir="$scratch"

+# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
+# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
+fb_parse() {
+  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
+  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
+  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
+  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
+  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
   118	    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
   119	    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
   120	    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
   122	    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
   123	    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
   124	    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
   125	    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
   126	    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
   127	    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
   128	    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
   129	     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
   130	     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
   131	    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
   132	    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
   133	        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
   134	        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
   135	        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
   136	        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
   137	        else . end)) as $knobs |
   138	    {
   139	      schema_version: 1,
   140	      id: $id,
   141	      profile: $sel.name,
   142	      profile_source: $sel.source,
   143	      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
   144	      profile_keys: $keys,
   145	      knobs: $knobs,
   146	      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
   147	                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
   148	                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
   149	      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
   150	                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
   151	    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
   152	  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
   153	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
   154	    return 1
   155	  fi
   156	  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
   157	  local w
   158	  while IFS= read -r w; do
   159	    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
   160	  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
   161	  return 0
   162	}
   163	
   164	_loa_pl_write_cache() {
   165	  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
   166	  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
   167	  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
   168	  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
   169	    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
   170	  fi
   171	  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
   172	  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   173	    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   174	  else
   175	    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   176	  fi
   177	  return 0
   178	}
   179	
   180	# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
   181	# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
   182	_loa_pl_load() {
   183	  _loa_pl_paths
   184	  _loa_pl_id
   185	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
   186	    return 0
   187	  fi
   188	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
   189	  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
   190	    local j
   191	    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
   192	        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
   193	    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
   194	      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
   195	      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   196	      return 0
   197	    fi
   198	  fi
   199	  _loa_pl_build || return 1
   200	  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
   201	  _loa_pl_write_cache
   202	  return 0
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
   206	_loa_pl_live() {
   207	  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
   208	  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   209	    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
   210	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   211	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   212	      return 0
   213	    fi
   214	  fi
   215	  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   216	  return 0
   217	}
   218	
   219	loa_knob() {
   220	  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
   221	  key="${path#.}"
   222	  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
   223	    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
   224	    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
   225	    return 2
   226	  fi
   227	  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
   228	  _loa_pl_paths
   229	  _loa_pl_id
   230	  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
   231	     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   232	    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
   233	          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
   234	            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   235	               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   236	             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
   237	          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
   238	    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   239	      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   240	      return 0
   241	    fi
   242	    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
   243	      printf '%s\n' "$v"
   244	      return 0
   245	    fi
   246	  fi
   247	  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
   248	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   249	    return 0
   250	  fi
   251	  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
   252	        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
   253	          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
   254	        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
   255	  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
   256	    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
   257	    return 0
   258	  fi
   259	  printf '%s\n' "$v"
   260	  return 0
   261	}
   262	
   263	loa_profile() {
   264	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   265	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
   266	  else
   267	    echo standard
   268	  fi
   269	  return 0
   270	}
   271	
   272	loa_profile_source() {
   273	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   274	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
   275	  else
   276	    echo default
   277	  fi
   278	  return 0
   279	}
   280	
   281	loa_profile_overrides() {
   282	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   283	    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
   284	  fi
   285	  return 0
   286	}
   287	
   288	loa_effective_json() {
   289	  if _loa_pl_load; then
   290	    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
   291	  else
   292	    echo '{}'
   293	  fi
   294	  return 0
   295	}
   296	
   297	if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
   298	  export LC_ALL=C
   299	  case "${1:-}" in
   300	    profile)   loa_profile ;;
   301	    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
   302	    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
   303	               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
   304	    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
   305	    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
   306	    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
   307	  esac
   308	fi
     1	# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
     2	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
     3	#
     4	# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
     5	# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
     6	# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
     7	#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
     8	#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
     9	#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
    10	#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
    11	#
    12	# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
    13	# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
    14	# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
    15	# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
    16	#
    17	# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
    18	# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
    19	# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
    20	# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
    21	# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
    22	schema_version: 1
    23	
    24	profiles:
    25	  lean:
    26	    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    27	    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    28	    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: false
    29	    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false
    30	    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    31	    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    32	    invisible_retrospective.enabled: false
    33	    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    34	    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
    35	  standard:

    37	    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    38	    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    39	    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    40	    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    41	    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    42	    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    43	    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    44	    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
    45	  full:
    46	    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
    47	    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    48	    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    49	    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true

     6	# `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds the run position from files: one case per
     7	# decision-table row, the breaker recompute from the feedback history, the
     8	# write path and its rollback knob, and one case per known reader over a
     9	# derived file. Fixture: a tiny git repo with a ledger, a2a/ and .run/ in a
    10	# temp dir; nothing touches this checkout's .run/.
    11	# =============================================================================

    13	setup() {
    14	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"

    16	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcd.XXXXXX")"
    17	  R="$T/repo"
    18	  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a" "$R/.run" "$R/src"
    19	  git -C "$R" init -q
    20	  printf 'x\n' > "$R/src/a.ts"
    21	  git -C "$R" add -A
    22	  git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm "feat: impl"
    23	  ledger completed completed completed
    24	  unset LOA_RUN_DIR LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE
    25	}
    26	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

    28	# ledger STATUS101 STATUS102 STATUS103 [EXTRA-SPRINT-JSON]
    29	ledger() {
    30	  jq -n --arg a "$1" --arg b "$2" --arg c "$3" --argjson x "${4:-null}" '
    31	    {schema_version: 1, active_cycle: "cycle-x", next_sprint_number: 104,
    32	     cycles: [
    33	       {id: "cycle-old", status: "archived", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    34	        sprints: [{global_id: 1, local_label: "sprint-1", status: "completed", created: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]},
    35	       {id: "cycle-x", status: "active", created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    36	        sprints: ([{global_id: 101, local_label: "sprint-1", status: $a, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    37	                   {global_id: 102, local_label: "sprint-2", status: $b, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    38	                   {global_id: 103, local_label: "sprint-3", status: $c, created: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]
    39	                  + (if $x == null then [] else [$x] end))}]}' > "$R/grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    40	}
    41	
    42	# feedback GID GATE VERDICT [SPRINT_ID] [ROUND] [MEDIUM] [TS] — a feedback file whose trailer verdict-derive accepts
    43	feedback() {
    44	  local gid="$1" gate="$2" verdict="$3" sid="${4:-sprint-$1}" round="${5:-}" med="${6:-0}" ts="${7:-2026-06-01T00:00:00Z}" f prose
    45	  mkdir -p "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid"
    46	  if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then f=engineer-feedback; else f=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
    47	  [[ -n "$round" ]] && f="$f-r$round"
    48	  if [[ "$verdict" == APPROVED ]]; then
    49	    if [[ "$gate" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    50	  else
    51	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: something to fix'
    52	  fi
    53	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"%s","ts":"%s"} -->\n' \
    54	    "$prose" "$gate" "$verdict" "$med" "$sid" "$ts" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$gid/$f.md"
    55	}
    56	
    57	# complete GID [SPRINT_ID] — review + audit APPROVED and the COMPLETED marker
    58	complete() {
    59	  feedback "$1" review APPROVED "${2:-}"
    60	  feedback "$1" audit APPROVED "${2:-}"
    61	  printf 'COMPLETED 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z\nsprint: %s\n' "${2:-sprint-$1}" > "$R/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-$1/COMPLETED"
    62	}
    63	
    64	# cache STATE [AGE_HOURS] [EXTRA-JQ] — .run/sprint-plan-state.json (jq now: portable, no GNU date -d)
    65	cache() {
    66	  jq -n --arg s "$1" --argjson h "${2:-0}" '
    67	    {schema_version: 2, plan_id: "plan-x", branch: "feature/x", state: $s,
    68	     timestamps: {started: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", last_activity: (now - $h * 3600 | floor | todate)},
    69	     sprints: {total: 3, completed: 0, current: "sprint-1",
    70	               list: [{id: "sprint-1", status: "in_progress"}, {id: "sprint-2", status: "pending"}, {id: "sprint-3", status: "pending"}]}}
    71	    '"${3:+| $3}" > "$R/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
    72	}

    74	derive() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" derive --root "$R" "$@"; }
    75	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
     5	# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
     6	# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
     7	# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
     8	# All files live in a temp dir.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    13	  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
    14	  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
    16	  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
    17	  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
    18	  S="$T/.run/state.json"
    19	  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
    20	}
    21	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    22	
    23	# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
    24	fb() {
    25	  local prose
    26	  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
    27	    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    28	  else
    29	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
    30	  fi
    31	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
    32	    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
    33	}
    34	
    35	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
    36	
    37	breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
    38	  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
    39	          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
    40	                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
    41	          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
    42	}
    43	
    44	rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
    45	
    46	@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
    47	  breaker
    48	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
    49	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    50	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    51	  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
    52	  local want
    53	  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
    54	  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
    55	  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
    56	  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
    57	}
    58

input.command: cd /workspace/pr; sed -n 85,380p head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh

content.content:
# Sprint-108 T4.5: Path normalization
# =============================================================================

# Read tool input from stdin (not for --effective-mode, which reads no payload)
input=""
if [[ "${1:-}" != "--effective-mode" ]]; then
    input=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || input=""
fi

# The ask reply; jq builds it so any reason is a well-formed JSON string (run-3 finding 7); the printf literal is only
# for the jq-missing branch, whose reason is a fixed string
emit_ask() {
    if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
        jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"ask",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
    else
        printf '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"%s"}}\n' "$1"
    fi
}

# Byte sequences strip_controls removes: UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80..C2 9F) and the format/bidi code points
# U+200B-U+200F, U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+2064, U+2066-U+206F, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+061C, U+180E, U+FE00-U+FE0F,
# U+FFF9-U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0001, U+E0020-U+E007F (run-3 finding 5); each sequence starts with a lead
# byte, so a byte-wise match never lands inside another character
# printf -v keeps this portable (no GNU-sed \x); built on first use, not on every Write/Edit (BB-008)
_IG_STRIP_SEQS=()
_ig_strip_seqs_init() {
    local _ig_i _ig_hex _ig_seq
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 160; _ig_i++ )); do
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xc2\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in 8b 8c 8d 8e 8f a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_hex in a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a6 a7 a8 a9 aa ab ac ad ae af; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "\\xe2\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for _ig_seq in '\xef\xbb\xbf' '\xc2\xad' '\xd8\x9c' '\xe1\xa0\x8e' '\xef\xbf\xb9' '\xef\xbf\xba' '\xef\xbf\xbb' '\xf3\xa0\x80\x81'; do
        printf -v _ig_seq "$_ig_seq"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 144; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+FE00-U+FE0F = EF B8 80..EF B8 8F
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xef\\xb8\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 160; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0020-U+E003F = F3 A0 80 A0..F3 A0 80 BF
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x80\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
    for (( _ig_i = 128; _ig_i < 192; _ig_i++ )); do   # U+E0040-U+E007F = F3 A0 81 80..F3 A0 81 BF
        printf -v _ig_hex '%02x' "$_ig_i"; printf -v _ig_seq "\\xf3\\xa0\\x81\\x${_ig_hex}"; _IG_STRIP_SEQS+=("$_ig_seq")
    done
}

# Sets the variable named $1 to at most 256 bytes of $2, never ending inside a UTF-8 character: a trailing lead byte
# whose sequence the cut left short, or stray continuation bytes, are dropped (run-3 finding 5; jq would read a split
# character as U+FFFD). printf -v, not $(...), so a trailing newline in a raw value survives into the audit row
cut_utf8_256() {
    local LC_ALL=C
    local _c_s=${2:0:256} _c_n _c_i _c_b _c_need
    _c_n=${#_c_s}
    for (( _c_i = _c_n - 1; _c_i >= 0 && _c_i >= _c_n - 4; _c_i-- )); do
        printf -v _c_b '%d' "'${_c_s:_c_i:1}"
        (( _c_b >= 128 && _c_b < 192 )) && continue   # continuation byte: keep walking back to its lead
        if (( _c_b < 128 )); then _c_need=1; elif (( _c_b < 224 )); then _c_need=2; elif (( _c_b < 240 )); then _c_need=3; else _c_need=4; fi
        if (( _c_n - _c_i < _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i}          # the cut left this character short
        elif (( _c_n - _c_i > _c_need )); then _c_s=${_c_s:0:_c_i+_c_need}   # continuation bytes after a complete character are stray
        fi
        printf -v "$1" '%s' "$_c_s"
        return 0
    done
    printf -v "$1" '%s' "${_c_s:0:_c_i+1}"   # only continuation bytes at the end: drop them
}

# Display copy of a model-authored string: cut to 256 bytes first (the fixed point below then costs at most a few
# passes over a short string), then C0 and DEL, then the sequences above byte-wise until nothing changes (deleting
# one sequence can join its neighbours into another: C2 C2 9B 9B)
strip_controls() {
    local LC_ALL=C s prev seq
    cut_utf8_256 s "$1"
    s=$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')
    (( ${#_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]} )) || _ig_strip_seqs_init
    while :; do
        prev=$s
        for seq in "${_IG_STRIP_SEQS[@]}"; do s=${s//"$seq"/}; done
        [[ "$s" == "$prev" ]] && break
    done
    printf '%s' "$s"
}

# The root never follows the process cwd, which follows Claude's `cd` (sprint-250 audit MED-001): PROJECT_ROOT, then
# the harness's CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (it stays at the session's project root), then this script's own location
# (<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/)
PROJECT_ROOT="${PROJECT_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)}}"
RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.run}"
FEATURES_FILE="$RUN_DIR/platform-features.json"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mode and claims (cycle-129 D-4.1): one yq call, read only when a decision
# needs it. Unset, unreadable or unknown values are ask; the legacy
# mode: authoritative is ask + claims: authoritative. run_mode.stale_hours
# bounds derived_at (positive integer, default 12).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
gate_mode="ask"
gate_claims="plain"
gate_stale_hours=12
load_gate_config() {
    local cfg="${1:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml}" raw m c s
    command -v yq &>/dev/null && command -v jq &>/dev/null && [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || return 0
    # mikefarah yq v4 first; the python yq wrapper (jq syntax, JSON out) second
    raw=$(yq -o json -I 0 '{"m": .implement_gate.mode, "c": .implement_gate.claims, "s": .run_mode.stale_hours}' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null) \
        || raw=$(yq -c '{"m": .implement_gate.mode, "c": .implement_gate.claims, "s": .run_mode.stale_hours}' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null) \
        || return 0
    m=$(jq -r '.m | strings' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || m=""
    c=$(jq -r '.c | strings' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || c=""
    s=$(jq -r '.s | numbers | tostring' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null) || s=""
    case "$m" in
        ask|telemetry|deny) gate_mode="$m" ;;
        authoritative) gate_claims="authoritative" ;;
    esac
    [[ "$c" == "authoritative" ]] && gate_claims="authoritative"
    if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] && (( 10#$s > 0 && 10#$s <= 8760 )); then gate_stale_hours=$(( 10#$s )); fi
    return 0
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--effective-mode" ]]; then
    load_gate_config "${2:-}"
    if [[ "$gate_claims" == "authoritative" ]]; then echo "$gate_mode (claims: authoritative)"; else echo "$gate_mode"; fi
    exit 0
fi

# Row helpers: LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 marks every row this gate writes (DEC-0167)
_ig_replay_json='{}'
[[ "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" == "1" ]] && _ig_replay_json='{"replay":true}'

# Evidence recorder: lead session only (no teammate role, no subagent agent_id), once, atomic.
if [[ -z "${LOA_TEAM_MEMBER:-}" && -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] \
    && jq -e '(.tool_input.active_skill // "") != "" and (.agent_id // "") == ""' <<<"$input" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && ! jq -e '.active_skill_seen_at' "$FEATURES_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ig_base=$(jq -c 'select(type == "object")' "$FEATURES_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
    _ig_tmp=$(mktemp "$RUN_DIR/.platform-features.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) && {
        jq -nc --argjson b "${_ig_base:-{\}}" --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
            '$b + {active_skill_available: false, active_skill_seen_at: $ts, active_skill_source: "tool_input"}' > "$_ig_tmp" 2>/dev/null \
            && mv -f "$_ig_tmp" "$FEATURES_FILE" 2>/dev/null
        rm -f "$_ig_tmp" 2>/dev/null
    }
fi

# No jq, or a payload jq cannot parse: the write cannot be evaluated, so ask (run-2 finding 5)
if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null || ! jq -e . <<<"$input" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input (jq missing or payload unparsable)." >&2
    emit_ask "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input. Verify this write is intentional."
    exit 0
fi

# Extract the path: Write/Edit/MultiEdit carry file_path, NotebookEdit carries notebook_path. jq -j plus a sentinel
# byte keeps a trailing newline, which $(...) would otherwise strip from the raw value (run-3 finding 4)
if ! file_path=$(jq -j '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.notebook_path // empty' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null && printf x); then
    echo "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input (path not readable)." >&2
    emit_ask "[GATE] could not evaluate tool_input. Verify this write is intentional."
    exit 0
fi
file_path=${file_path%x}

# A parsed payload without a path is not a file write the gate can classify: allow
if [[ -z "$file_path" ]]; then
    exit 0
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source compat-lib.sh for _date_to_epoch()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd 2>/dev/null)" || SCRIPT_DIR=""
COMPAT_LIB="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../scripts/compat-lib.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/compat-lib.sh
source "$COMPAT_LIB" 2>/dev/null || true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# T4.5: Path normalization — canonicalise both sides, then take file_path
# relative to the project root (run-2 finding 1). A textual prefix test let
# /proc/self/cwd/src/x, //ROOT/src/x, ROOT/../<name>/src/x or a symlinked root
# reach an App-Zone file unseen. Two forms are tested and either one matching
# counts (run-3 finding 1): the PHYSICAL form follows symlinks (realpath -m,
# else readlink -f) against pwd -P of the root; the LOGICAL form keeps them
# (realpath -m -s, else a pure-bash ./../// normaliser) against pwd -L, so a
# src/ that is itself a symlink out of the root still asks. A relative path
# resolves from the payload's cwd when it carries one (the harness resolves it
# there and cwd follows `cd` in the Bash tool), else from PROJECT_ROOT (run-3
# finding 6). Only the part under the root is matched, so parent directory
# names never count (e.g., /home/user/src-projects/loa/grimoires/file.md is not src/*).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lexical normaliser for an absolute path: drops empty and . components, resolves .. textually, follows no symlink
_ig_lexical_norm() {
    local rest=$1 part
    local -a out=()
    while [[ -n "$rest" ]]; do
        part=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ "$rest" == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=""; fi
        case "$part" in
            ''|.) ;;
            ..) (( ${#out[@]} )) && unset 'out[${#out[@]}-1]' ;;
            *) out+=("$part") ;;
        esac
    done
    local IFS=/
    printf '/%s' "${out[*]}"
}

# $1 relative to the root $2, or failure when $1 is not under $2
_ig_under_root() {
    [[ "$1" == "${2%/}/"* ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "${1#"${2%/}"/}"
}

canonical_root=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || canonical_root=""
logical_root=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -L) || logical_root=""
payload_cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // empty | strings' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null) || payload_cwd=""
if [[ "$file_path" == /* ]]; then
    abs_path=$file_path
else
    base_dir=${payload_cwd:-$logical_root}
    [[ "$base_dir" == /* ]] || base_dir="$logical_root/$base_dir"
    abs_path="${base_dir%/}/$file_path"
fi
canonical_path=""
logical_path=""
if [[ -n "$canonical_root" && -n "$logical_root" ]]; then
    # GNU realpath -m first (no component needs to exist), then readlink -f
    canonical_path=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null \
        && { realpath -m -- "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null || readlink -f -- "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null; }) || canonical_path=""
    logical_path=$(realpath -m -s -- "$abs_path" 2>/dev/null) || logical_path=""
    [[ "$logical_path" == /* ]] || logical_path=$(_ig_lexical_norm "$abs_path")
fi
if [[ -z "$canonical_root" || -z "$canonical_path" ]]; then
    echo "[GATE] could not canonicalise tool_input.file_path; asking." >&2
    emit_ask "[GATE] could not canonicalise tool_input.file_path. Verify this write is intentional."
    exit 0
fi

# The root-relative forms, lowercased: on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default, ext4 casefold) Src/ is src/,
# and on a case-sensitive one this only adds asks for a directory literally named Src/ — tighten-only (run-3 finding 2)
# bash 3.2 has no lowercase parameter expansion (BB-001: a bad substitution there left rel_forms empty and the hook exited 0); LC_ALL=C so a
# BSD tr never stops at a byte that is not valid UTF-8 ("Illegal byte sequence") — the patterns are ASCII
_ig_lower() { printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }
rel_forms=()
if rel=$(_ig_under_root "$canonical_path" "$canonical_root"); then rel_forms+=("$(_ig_lower "$rel")"); fi
if rel=$(_ig_under_root "$logical_path" "$logical_root"); then rel_forms+=("$(_ig_lower "$rel")"); fi

# Audit-row copy of a model-authored value: raw, cut to 256 bytes on a character boundary; jq -a escapes the rest
cut_utf8_256 audit_file_path "$file_path"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trust inputs (run-3 finding 3): the files this gate and the run state read are
# writable through the same tool, so a write to one asks and leaves one
# compliance.state_write row — evaluated before the App-Zone test, since they
# are not App Zone. Everything else under .run/ and grimoires/ stays allow.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
for rel in "${rel_forms[@]}"; do
    case "$rel" in
        .run/state.json|.run/sprint-plan-state.json|.run/simstim-state.json|.run/platform-features.json|.run/audit.jsonl|.run/implement-active.json|.loa.config.yaml)
            echo "[GATE] write to an implement-gate trust input '$(strip_controls "$file_path")'." >&2
            # Asks in every mode and under every sanction; the row is counted as an ask by the register
            load_gate_config
            jq -nca \
                --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" \
                --arg path "$audit_file_path" \
                --arg mode "$gate_mode" \
                --argjson replay "$_ig_replay_json" \
                '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.state_write", file_path: $path,
                  hook: "implement-gate", action: "ask", decision: "trust_input", mode: $mode} + $replay' \
                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
            emit_ask "[GATE] write to an implement-gate trust input. Verify this write is intentional."
            exit 0
            ;;
    esac
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Zone check: Is this an App Zone write?
# App Zone: src/, lib/, app/ in either root-relative form; a path whose two
# forms both fall outside the root is not App Zone
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
is_app_zone=false
for normalized_path in "${rel_forms[@]}"; do
    case "$normalized_path" in
        src/*|lib/*|app/*|*/src/*|*/lib/*|*/app/*)
            is_app_zone=true
            ;;
    esac
done

# Non-App-Zone writes always allowed
if [[ "$is_app_zone" == "false" ]]; then
    exit 0
fi

# Display copy only: control and format characters never reach stderr (n21, run-2 finding 3)
